newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB's Hehn sees durum exports as top challenge.
newsitem.headline: CWB's Hehn sees durum exports as top challenge.

text.p: Exporting durum wheat will likely be the Canadian Wheat Board's most challenging task in marketing year 1996/97 (Aug/July) given low supplies and political uncertainties, the head of the agency said.

"The biggest challenge we're going to face is on the durum wheat side. We're carrying a small amount of durum wheat in from last year and the big market is in North Africa and the political climate there is still very unstable," CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn told Reuters.
Agriculture Canada estimated durum carry-in for 1996/97 at 1.8 million tonnes, up from 1.46 million the previous year.
Statistics Canada pegged durum production in 1996/97 at 4.36 million, down from 4.73 million the previous year.
Canada exported 1.13 million tonnes of durum to Algeria in 1995/96, Canadian Grain Commission statistics show.
Algeria, the CWB's largest durum customer, imported 1.89 million tonnes in 1994/95, CGC figures show.
Canada exported 223,000 tonnes to Morocco in 1995/96.
North African durum production was widely expected to be double that of the previous year's drought-cut output, thereby reducing demand in the world's largest importing region.
